text:
Aisha: quick heads-up — saw ~12-18% host CPU increase for the fronting proxy after yesterday's kernel selector change. p50 decode latency bumped ~6ms under 512B requests.
Leo: ouch. which path is burning CPU? gRPC, parsing, tokenization?
Aisha: mostly request parsing and framing (HTTP2 hpack decode, header copies). grpc write path also shows a lot of small syscalls. KV cache hit-rate slightly down but I think it's orthogonal.
Raj: can you paste the flame snippet?
Aisha: pasted below from `perf top` on the worker node (short capture):
```
  23.4%  libprotobuf.so      http2_parser::decode_headers
  17.1%  runtime-proxy       parse_request_line
  12.0%  libc.so             writev
   8.9%  http2               hpack_decode_table_lookup
   7.5%  runtime-proxy       allocate_header_buffer
```
Maya: that `allocate_header_buffer` looks like repeated allocations on every stream. are we copying headers into a new buffer per chunk?
Aisha: yes, the host-side framing creates a small vector per incoming frame -> then we append into a string for tokenizer. lots of short-lived allocations.
Leo: two obvious levers: buffer pooling + avoid double-copy when piping frames into tokenizer. also consider coalescing small frames before handing to parse layer.
Raj: could we do an in-place hpack decode into preallocated slab? then tokenizer reads from slab without allocation.
Maya: agreed, a slab + per-connection arena would kill many alloc hotspots. also we should check writev batching to combine small gRPC chunks — writev % is high.
Aisha: repro steps I used: `wrk -c200 -t4 -d60 --header "content-type: application/grpc" /v1/predict` with a payload of 512B; capture perf and `eBPF` stack traces.
infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary 2026-03-18T07:08 by raj -> host-proxy-v2-kernel-selector
Leo: timeline: if we do slab pooling + reuse header buffers, I think we can recover ~8-10% CPU. coalescing gRPC writes could shave another 5%.
Raj: picked this up as a regression in commit `a3f2b9` (kernel selection heuristics) — it swapped in a new decode path that returns more small frames to the host frontend.
Maya: so the kernel change increased fragmentation upstream. two-pronged fix: revert or add host optimizations. prefer host fix for long-term.
Aisha: working on a small PoC: prealloc 8KB buffer per connection, in-place hpack decode into it, and a tokenization shim that points into that buffer (no copy). early micro-bench: p50 parse latency down 3.6ms.
Leo: can you share the patch when ready? include microbench script, and a toggle flag (env) so we can roll.
Aisha: will open PR today. also want to try batching parse events at ingress: if small frames arrive within 2ms, merge before decoding.
Raj: watch out for tail-latency tradeoffs — 2ms merge window helps throughput but could bump p99 for single-request flows. add metrics to measure p50/p95/p99 separately.
Maya: also check KV cache interaction — if we delay parse by merging, maybe we reduce early KV prefetch hits. need a small experiment to measure kvcache hit-rate with/without merge.
Aisha: good point. my initial perf run kept kvcache steady but I'll run the merge test.
Leo: another low-hanging: avoid copying headers into std::string when building request proto; parse directly from iovecs where possible.
Aisha: noted. action items: (1) Aisha PoC pool + in-place HPACK (PR), (2) Aisha run merge-window experiment and measure kvcache hit-rate, (3) Leo add writev coalescing on gRPC outbound, (4) Raj add canary flag and perf regression alert if host CPU > baseline +8%.
Raj: tagging oncall to watch the canary tonight @Maya.
Maya: on it, will watch dashboards and flamegraphs. :eyes:
Aisha: I'll post PR link and microbench results once tests run. thanks all. :thumbsup:
